Jamie: Quick announcement — we're changing the release train cadence and updating the deploy playbook. Read before EOD please.
Alejandro: ok — what specifically is changing?
Jamie: High level: move to a 3-week train (instead of 2-week), with a shorter hard freeze window. Purpose: fewer small partial rollouts, more predictable canaries + capacity planning.
Marie: How does this affect canaries and rollback thresholds?
Jamie: Canary windows for model-serving routes increase from 30m -> 45m for any shard with avg QPS > 100. Rollback threshold is unchanged (error rate spike > 3% OR latency p95 > baseline + 300ms).
Lina: Will this change the quiet/freezes schedule?
Jamie: Yes — new pattern: Week A = dev + small features, Week B = scheduled major rollouts (canary + ramp), Week C = stabilization & emergency-only hotfixes. Hard freeze starts 6 hours before canary start for Week B.
Sam: Is there a config snippet we should update in infra manifests?
Jamie: Yup, please update deploy_policy in service manifests. Example (copy/paste):
```
rollout_policy:
  canary_duration: "45m"
  initial_traffic: "10%"
  ramp_steps: ["10%","30%","60%","100%"]
  rollback_on:
    error_rate_percent: 3
    latency_p95_ms_delta: 300
```
Priya: Heads-up for PMs — releases that touch embeddings or quant plugins should get a two-day preflight note to infra and perf. Otherwise they'll get queued to Week B.
Marie: Exceptions? We still have the freeze-exception process, right?
Jamie: Yes. If you need an exception, file the exception request form and tag @Priya + @Alejandro. Requests must include canary plan, perf regression checks, and a rollback timeline. Link: https://redwood.internal/forms/release-exception
Alejandro: I'll update the console deploy docs and add the new canary timer to the default templates.
deploy-bot: Reminder: next scheduled canary window for staging -> prod is Tue 14:00 UTC (old cadence). That will move to Tue 11:00 UTC starting next cycle.
Lina: Will oncall shifts change for the longer canaries?
Priya: Minor change — primary oncall covers the whole canary, secondary only for escalation after first 30m. We'll update the rota.
Sam: Any changes to SLA for Dedicated customers?
Jamie: No SLA changes. This is an ops/process change to reduce regressions and improve rollout visibility.
Marie: Cool. When does this start?
Jamie: Starting next Monday (cycle start). We'll run a 1-week pilot with the infra team this week — please expect a brief retro on Friday.
Lina: Thanks — I'll notify the docs owners and create the PR to change the templates.
Alejandro: Will add a small testsuite to CI that asserts the canary_duration field is present and >= 45m for model-serving services.
Priya: Thanks all. If you want a walk-through, I'll host a 30m sync tomorrow 10:30am UTC — invite incoming. :calendar: :eyes:
Sam: +1 attending.
Marie: joining.
Jamie: Appreciated. Quick TL;DR at the top of the playbook has been added: https://redwood.internal/docs/deploy-playbook#release-cadence-update
Alejandro: noted.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled trigger (preview): service=embed-service shard=eu-west-1 planned_duration=45m
Jamie: ok that matches. If anything blocks your workstreams ping me or @Priya in this thread. :thumbsup:
